rows.title: A Model to Limit Batching Denial of Service Attacks on GraphQL
rows.authors: Arno MOLLER; Sheunesu M. Makura; Hein S. Venter
rows.abstract: GraphQL is a dynamic API data query and manipulation language created by Facebook and made open source in 2015. A standout feature of GraphQL is batching, which allows multiple queries of varying complexity to be combined into a single query request. However, this feature makes GraphQL vulnerable to denial-of-service attacks. This paper aims to limit the effect of DoS attacks through a hybrid static/dynamic query cost analysis approach. rows.title: WENDIGO: Deep Reinforcement Learning for Denial-of-Service Query Discovery in GraphQL
rows.authors: Shae McFadden; Marcello Maugeri; Chris Hicks; Vasilios Mavroudis
rows.abstract: GraphQL is a type of web API which enables a unified endpoint for an application’s resources through its own query language, and is widely adopted by companies such as Meta, GitHub, X, and PayPal. The query-based structure of GraphQL is designed to reduce the over-/under-fetching typical of REST web APIs. Consequently, GraphQL allows attackers to perform Denial-of-Service (DoS) attacks through queries inducing higher server loads with fewer requests. rows.abstract: GraphQL is a query language that allows clients to request specific data from an API, making it more efficient and flexible compared to traditional REST APIs. This makes applications faster and more efficient by reducing data over-fetching, combining various data sources into a single request, and supporting schema changes without disrupting the integrity of existing applications. rows.title: Model for Dynamic Input Validation for Graph Query Language (GraphQL)
rows.venue: Journal of Artificial Intelligence and Emerging Technologies
rows.authors: Beauty Nuka* Nwile; Daniel Matthias; Vincent I.E. Anireh; Onate E. Taylor
rows.abstract: This study presents the design and evaluation of an improved input validation architecture for Graph Query Language (GraphQL), addressing key issues in performance, security, and scalability within GraphQL environments. With the increasing adoption of GraphQL in API-driven systems, effective input validation is critical to mitigate security vulnerabilities, optimize query efficiency, and enhance system robustness. rows.title: Microservice architecture patterns with GraphQL
rows.abstract: In this thesis the GraphQL query language was studied in the context of the microservice architecture. The thesis was a combination of a literary study and expert interviews. Most prevalent microservice architecture patterns were gathered from peer reviewed studies and grey literature. Four expert interviews were held to detect which patterns were used in projects which used a microservice architecture and GraphQL APIs. Based on the interviews, a typical GraphQL microservice architecture consists of up to 10 REST or GraphQL microservices exposed to public networks using a GraphQL API gateway.

rows.abstract: GraphQL query cost analysis is widely used to protect APIs from excessive resource consumption and denial-of-service attacks. However, existing approaches often fail to accurately reflect actual system load and provide limited guidance for tool selection, configuration, and interpretation of predicted costs across different query categories.
